title: Thermal history limits a feasible burst
question: Why can the same electrically feasible current leave different thermal margins?
scope: Dimensionless first-order thermal example, not the motor data sheet or a qualification model. Low-speed electrical feasibility is assumed. Ambient rise is zero, burst equilibrium is two, and the insulation threshold is one. Time is normalized by the thermal time constant.

steps.title: Initial temperature persists
steps.explanation: A winding begins with retained thermal state.

snapshot.result: The winding retains its initial heat before the burst begins.

steps.title: Apply a feasible current burst
steps.explanation: Current changes immediately; temperature remains continuous.

snapshot.result: Current is on, but the winding has not instantaneously heated.

transition.meaning: Current changes immediately; temperature remains continuous.

steps.title: Heat the winding for one interval
steps.explanation: The first-order thermal state integrates heating over a bounded interval.

snapshot.result: Stored heat has increased.

transition.meaning: The first-order thermal state integrates heating over a bounded interval.

steps.title: Continue the same current
steps.explanation: The unchanged current continues generating heat.

snapshot.result: The continuing burst crosses the threshold even though the current remains electrically feasible.

transition.meaning: The unchanged current continues generating heat.

steps.title: Remove burst current
steps.explanation: Removing current stops the modeled heat input; it does not erase stored heat.

snapshot.result: Current is off, but the winding remains above the insulation threshold.

transition.meaning: Removing current stops the modeled heat input; it does not erase stored heat.

steps.title: Cool with current removed
steps.explanation: The winding loses heat toward ambient over one normalized time interval.

snapshot.result: Cooling reduces stored heat; removing current did not erase the thermal history.

transition.meaning: The winding loses heat toward ambient over one normalized time interval.

invariants: Temperature is continuous when current switches.
Removing current leaves stored heat; cooling takes time.
The thermal model does not replace the torque-speed voltage envelope.

title: Stored supply outlasts permission
question: Why can execution stop while the chunk still contains future setpoints?
scope: Toy direct-replacement schedule with eight capture-relative slots, arrival at tick two, evidence expiry at tick five, and lease expiry at tick six. These abstract ticks do not replace the chapter clock or its machine parameters. No temporal ensembling is modeled.

steps.title: Capture an observation
steps.explanation: Capture starts an independent evidence clock.

snapshot.result: Capture has started inference; no setpoints have arrived.

steps.title: Receive the computed chunk
steps.explanation: The capture-relative prefix has already elapsed and cannot be replayed.

snapshot.result: The received chunk keeps its future supply, but its elapsed prefix cannot execute.

transition.meaning: The capture-relative prefix has already elapsed and cannot be replayed.

steps.title: Execute setpoint u2
steps.explanation: One admitted setpoint executes while replacement inference remains unfinished.

snapshot.result: The first admitted setpoint has executed; later setpoints remain stored.

transition.meaning: One admitted setpoint executes while replacement inference remains unfinished.

steps.title: Execute setpoint u3
steps.explanation: One admitted setpoint executes while replacement inference remains unfinished.

snapshot.result: The next admitted setpoint has executed while replacement inference is still unfinished.

transition.meaning: One admitted setpoint executes while replacement inference remains unfinished.

steps.title: Execute setpoint u4
steps.explanation: One admitted setpoint executes while replacement inference remains unfinished.

snapshot.result: The final evidence-valid setpoint has executed before the expiry tick.

transition.meaning: One admitted setpoint executes while replacement inference remains unfinished.

steps.title: Deny execution at evidence expiry
steps.explanation: The next permission check refuses the remaining chunk even though future setpoints remain stored.

snapshot.result: Evidence has expired, so the next setpoint is denied despite the stored tail.

transition.meaning: The next permission check refuses the remaining chunk even though future setpoints remain stored.

steps.title: Expire the unrenewed lease
steps.explanation: Time advances without a newly admitted replacement; fallback retains control.

snapshot.result: The unrenewed lease has also expired; stored data grant no authority.

transition.meaning: Time advances without a newly admitted replacement; fallback retains control.

invariants: Elapsed setpoints are never replayed.
A further setpoint requires both valid evidence and a valid lease.
Stored supply cannot renew evidence or authority.

title: Reuse KV within one intent evaluation
question: Which state survives a decode read, and when does its ownership end?
scope: Schematic three-position camera/instruction prompt and two sampled tokens in one independent evaluation. KV means one position’s retained key/value pair across layers; tensor shapes and attention arithmetic are omitted.

objects.label: Evaluation A: camera and instruction tokens
Current decode input and read operands

steps.title: Begin one independent intent evaluation
steps.explanation: The observation and instruction belong to evaluation A; its cache starts empty.

snapshot.result: Evaluation A owns an empty cache; its prompt is ready.

steps.title: Prefill the observation and instruction
steps.explanation: One prefill processes all prompt positions and retains their keys and values.

snapshot.result: Prompt keys and values remain resident for later decode queries.

transition.meaning: One prefill processes all prompt positions and retains their keys and values.

steps.title: Sample the first output token
steps.explanation: The prefill output supports sampling a0; a0 has not yet been consumed.

snapshot.result: Output a0 exists, but its key and value are not yet in the cache.

transition.meaning: The prefill output supports sampling a0; a0 has not yet been consumed.

steps.title: Compute the next decode input state
steps.explanation: Decode consumes a0 and computes its query, key, and value.

snapshot.result: Decode has consumed a0 and computed its current-token state.

transition.meaning: Decode consumes a0 and computes its query, key, and value.

steps.title: Read retained prompt KV without eviction
steps.explanation: The current query reads the prior prompt positions; every source cache cell remains retained.

snapshot.result: Prompt KV remains resident while distinct read copies reach the decode workspace.

transition.meaning: The current query reads the prior prompt positions; every source cache cell remains retained.

steps.title: Append the consumed input token KV
steps.explanation: The cache grows by the key and value of a0, the current input token.

snapshot.result: KV(a0) is now retained because a0 was consumed as an input.

transition.meaning: The cache grows by the key and value of a0, the current input token.

steps.title: Sample the next output token
steps.explanation: Attention over prior and current KV supplies the decode output used to sample a1.

snapshot.result: Output a1 is sampled from the completed decode computation; it has not been cached.

transition.meaning: Attention over prior and current KV supplies the decode output used to sample a1.

steps.title: Finish evaluation A and release its KV
steps.explanation: After the evaluation completes and all consumers finish, its cache is released. The next independent observation requires new prefill.

snapshot.result: Evaluation A has ended. Its released cache cannot carry into the next independent observation.

transition.meaning: After the evaluation completes and all consumers finish, its cache is released. The next independent observation requires new prefill.

invariants: Reading KV does not evict it.
A sampled output is appended only after it becomes a consumed decode input.
Independent observations do not inherit this evaluation’s KV.

title: Consistent data can lose authority
question: Why can a whole mailbox snapshot still become ineligible to execute?
scope: MCU-local publication in event order, with two toy payload cells and abstract lease ticks. The AP sends framed transport; it does not share MCU memory. One tick makes one read attempt. Sequence numbers are identifiers, not timing.

objects.label: Checked frame in MCU receive memory

steps.title: Receive a checked frame beside the old mailbox
steps.explanation: The transport has delivered a complete frame into MCU-owned receive memory. The tick retains its complete prior proposal under its existing lease; no AP/MCU memory is shared.

snapshot.result: A complete received frame waits beside the old published mailbox and reader snapshot.

steps.title: Mark the publication sequence odd
steps.explanation: The writer marks the slot unavailable before mutating any payload cell.

snapshot.result: The odd counter forbids accepting the slot before its first payload cell changes.

transition.meaning: The writer marks the slot unavailable before mutating any payload cell.

steps.title: Copy the first payload cell
steps.explanation: The interrupt writer copies one cell while the sequence remains odd; this snapshot exposes the partial copy.

snapshot.result: The mailbox mixes old and new cells, so the odd counter forbids accepting it.

transition.meaning: The interrupt writer copies one cell while the sequence remains odd; this snapshot exposes the partial copy.

steps.title: Reject one odd-sequence read attempt
steps.explanation: A permission tick preempts the writer. Its one bounded attempt rejects the odd counter and retains the prior validated payload.

snapshot.result: The interrupted tick retains the complete old proposal and does not spin.

transition.meaning: A permission tick preempts the writer. Its one bounded attempt rejects the odd counter and retains the prior validated payload.

steps.title: Finish copying the payload
steps.explanation: Both new payload cells are present, but the odd sequence still marks the slot unpublished.

snapshot.result: The new payload is complete, but the odd counter still forbids acceptance.

transition.meaning: Both new payload cells are present, but the odd sequence still marks the slot unpublished.

steps.title: Publish the even sequence
steps.explanation: The interrupt writer completes publication after all payload writes.

snapshot.result: The even counter publishes the completed payload; the reader still holds its old snapshot.

transition.meaning: The interrupt writer completes publication after all payload writes.

steps.title: Accept a matching even read
steps.explanation: One bounded tick read observes the same even sequence before and after copying. The reader retains the complete candidate; admission has not yet renewed its authority.

snapshot.result: The reader now holds the whole new payload; consistency alone has not renewed authority.

transition.meaning: One bounded tick read observes the same even sequence before and after copying. The reader retains the complete candidate; admission has not yet renewed its authority.

steps.title: Admit the validated proposal
steps.explanation: A separate permission decision admits the complete fresh proposal and renews its lease. The even sequence alone was insufficient.

snapshot.result: Separate admission renews authority for the validated proposal.

transition.meaning: A separate permission decision admits the complete fresh proposal and renews its lease. The even sequence alone was insufficient.

steps.title: Expire authority during the proposer stall
steps.explanation: No new frame or admission arrives. An unchanged even payload remains consistent while its lease expires and fallback takes control.

snapshot.result: The mailbox remains whole, but its authority has expired. Fallback controls execution.

transition.meaning: No new frame or admission arrives. An unchanged even payload remains consistent while its lease expires and fallback takes control.

invariants: An odd sequence never replaces the reader’s last validated snapshot.
Payload copy completion precedes even publication.
Consistent repeated reads do not renew authority without a new admission.

title: One motion produces four distinct signals
question: Which causal stage supplies a supervised action target?
scope: Toy scalar mapping and clamp in normalized illustrative coordinates, with a separately declared measured response. The source’s four synchronized taps and separate AP/MCU memories are retained. No physical response law or expert eligibility is inferred.

objects.label: Synchronized tap tuple: asked / mapped / enforced / measured

steps.title: Issue the raw request
steps.explanation: A toy normalized request enters the unprivileged AP; its source is not an authority grant.

snapshot.result: Only raw intent is available; mapping and permission have not occurred.

steps.title: Map the request into command coordinates
steps.explanation: The declared scalar mapping multiplies the request by the toy conversion scale.

snapshot.result: The mapped command differs from the requested action because the coordinate mapping changes its value.

transition.meaning: The declared scalar mapping multiplies the request by the toy conversion scale.

steps.title: Deliver the framed command to MCU memory
steps.explanation: Black-channel transport delivers the mapped command to a separate MCU-owned receive endpoint.

snapshot.result: The MCU has received the mapped proposal, but it has not yet enforced its limit.

transition.meaning: Black-channel transport delivers the mapped command to a separate MCU-owned receive endpoint.

steps.title: Clamp the command at the permission path
steps.explanation: The toy amplitude bound limits the mapped proposal before dispatch. Passing this check does not certify expert demonstration quality.

snapshot.result: The enforced command is lower than the mapped proposal because the permission path clamps it.

transition.meaning: The toy amplitude bound limits the mapped proposal before dispatch. Passing this check does not certify expert demonstration quality.

steps.title: Dispatch the enforced command
steps.explanation: The admitted command reaches the drives; plant response remains unmeasured.

snapshot.result: The drive receives the enforced command; response remains to be measured.

transition.meaning: The admitted command reaches the drives; plant response remains unmeasured.

steps.title: Measure the plant response over the aligned interval
steps.explanation: The toy response is an independently declared observation, not a prediction from the scalar clamp.

snapshot.result: Measured response differs from the enforced command, preserving the evidence of tracking behavior.

transition.meaning: The toy response is an independently declared observation, not a prediction from the scalar clamp.

steps.title: Declare the supervised target tap
steps.explanation: This diagnostic example selects the enforced tap for comparison only; provenance and curation must still decide training eligibility.

snapshot.result: The target explicitly names the enforced tap. Its provenance still requires curation before training.

transition.meaning: This diagnostic example selects the enforced tap for comparison only; provenance and curation must still decide training eligibility.

invariants: Asked, mapped, enforced, and measured signals have distinct identities.
Measured response can differ from the drive command.
Permission enforcement does not automatically make a record an expert target.

title: Takeover provenance determines label eligibility
question: Why does a takeover leave several nearby commands masked?
scope: One fixed, eight-sample toy intervention trace in event order. Error values are illustrative normalized coordinates, not measured outcomes or a learning bound. Expert review is declared, not automated by the plot.

objects.label: Fixed captured states by event index

steps.title: Inspect one fixed intervention trace
steps.explanation: The toy trace has learner divergence, takeover blend, operator reorientation, and measured stabilization. Values are illustrative, not empirical drift data.

snapshot.result: All records remain pending; a takeover alone grants no expert label.

steps.title: Retain the pre-takeover divergent states
steps.explanation: The lookback includes learner-visited states that an expert may later relabel; learner commands remain excluded from expert targets.

snapshot.result: Divergent learner-visited states are retained for possible relabeling; their learner commands stay masked.

transition.meaning: The lookback includes learner-visited states that an expert may later relabel; learner commands remain excluded from expert targets.

steps.title: Mask the controller blend
steps.explanation: The enforcer’s transitional action remains diagnostic data with explicit provenance.

snapshot.result: The blend is explicitly excluded from expert targets despite following takeover.

transition.meaning: The enforcer’s transitional action remains diagnostic data with explicit provenance.

steps.title: Mask operator reorientation
steps.explanation: A human takeover does not immediately create a stabilized expert demonstration.

snapshot.result: Operator reorientation remains excluded until measured stabilization.

transition.meaning: A human takeover does not immediately create a stabilized expert demonstration.

steps.title: Mark measured stabilization
steps.explanation: Stabilization identifies a possible recovery segment; label eligibility still requires review.

snapshot.result: The stabilized recovery segment is a review candidate, not yet an expert target.

transition.meaning: Stabilization identifies a possible recovery segment; label eligibility still requires review.

steps.title: Admit only the reviewed recovery segment
steps.explanation: Explicit review admits the stabilized recovery commands while preserving all earlier masks.

snapshot.result: Only the explicitly reviewed recovery commands become expert targets; earlier masks remain in force.

transition.meaning: Explicit review admits the stabilized recovery commands while preserving all earlier masks.

invariants: Learner-visited states can be relabel eligible while their learner commands remain masked.
Blend and reorientation commands stay excluded from expert targets.
Stabilization precedes explicit review and admission of expert recovery.

title: Dependent refinement spends renewal slack
question: What changes while a new candidate is refined and an old chunk keeps executing?
scope: Toy fixed-seed interpolation between a declared noisy path and one demonstrated mode, not the numerical diffusion algorithm or measured latency. Event order shows dependent evaluations and separately admitted execution; obstacle center alone does not model its extent.

objects.label: AP candidate and fixed demonstrated modes

steps.title: Hold a noisy candidate beside the admitted chunk
steps.explanation: Two fixed demonstrated modes pass on opposite sides of a toy obstacle; their mean passes through its center.

snapshot.result: The noisy AP candidate has no authority; the MCU retains its separately admitted chunk.

steps.title: Complete the first dependent refinement
steps.explanation: A schematic fixed-seed interpolation moves the candidate toward one selected mode; it is not a diffusion solver.

snapshot.result: The first refinement changes the candidate while the active MCU chunk remains intact.

transition.meaning: A schematic fixed-seed interpolation moves the candidate toward one selected mode; it is not a diffusion solver.

steps.title: Execute one already admitted setpoint
steps.explanation: The MCU consumes u0 from its active chunk independently of unfinished AP candidate refinement.

snapshot.result: The MCU has consumed u0; this does not admit or advance the AP candidate.

transition.meaning: The MCU consumes u0 from its active chunk independently of unfinished AP candidate refinement.

steps.title: Complete the next dependent refinement
steps.explanation: The next refinement consumes the preceding candidate, so its evaluation cannot run before that input exists.

snapshot.result: The next dependent evaluation refines the preceding candidate.

transition.meaning: The next refinement consumes the preceding candidate, so its evaluation cannot run before that input exists.

steps.title: Execute the next admitted setpoint
steps.explanation: The active chunk keeps feeding the permission path while candidate computation spends renewal slack.

snapshot.result: The MCU has consumed u1 while the AP candidate remains unadmitted.

transition.meaning: The active chunk keeps feeding the permission path while candidate computation spends renewal slack.

steps.title: Finish the candidate refinement
steps.explanation: The final schematic candidate follows the selected demonstration mode; collision and actuator checks remain separate.

snapshot.result: Refinement has produced a coherent candidate, whose feasibility remains unverified.

transition.meaning: The final schematic candidate follows the selected demonstration mode; collision and actuator checks remain separate.

steps.title: Deliver the candidate for independent admission
steps.explanation: Transport places the candidate in MCU-owned memory. The active chunk is not replaced merely because a candidate arrived.

snapshot.result: The candidate has arrived in MCU memory pending admission. The old admitted chunk remains active.

transition.meaning: Transport places the candidate in MCU-owned memory. The active chunk is not replaced merely because a candidate arrived.

invariants: Each refinement consumes the previous candidate.
The MCU’s active chunk is distinct from the AP candidate.
Transport completion is not permission or active-buffer replacement.
